panels.description: Share of authentication requests faster than 250ms. Keycloak records the 250ms bucket because KC_HTTP_METRICS_SLOS includes 250. Authentication URIs are the templated protocol and login-actions routes.
panels.title: Auth latency SLO (<250ms)

panels.description: Share of authentication requests whose Micrometer outcome is SERVER_ERROR.
panels.title: Auth server error rate

panels.description: Successful user login events per second. The event label is lowercase. An empty error label means the event succeeded.
panels.title: Successful logins

panels.description: Failed user login events divided by all login events. Failures are the same login event with a non-empty error label, for example invalid_user_credentials.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(keycloak_user_events_total{job="$job", realm=~"$realm", event="login", error!=""}[5m])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min((sum(rate(keycloak_user_events_total{job="$job", realm=~"$realm", event="login"}[5m])) or vector(0)), 0.000001)

panels.title: Login failure ratio

panels.description: Active Agroal connections divided by active plus idle connections.
panels.title: DB pool usage

panels.description: In-flight HTTP requests on the Keycloak application listener.
panels.title: Active requests

panels.description: Successful logins in the time range. The keycloak-login-tracker service reads the realm's logins from Keycloak's event store every 30 s and writes them to Loki (service_name=keycloak-logins).
panels.title: Logins

panels.description: Failed logins (LOGIN_ERROR) in the time range: wrong password, unknown user, a failed second factor.
panels.title: Failed logins

panels.description: Logins flagged as impossible travel in the time range. Impossible travel: a successful login more than 300 km from the user's previous located login, which it could only have reached faster than 1000 km/h. New country: a successful login from a country the user has no located login from in the last 30 days, while it has some from others.
panels.title: Impossible travel

panels.description: Logins flagged as from a new country in the time range. Impossible travel: a successful login more than 300 km from the user's previous located login, which it could only have reached faster than 1000 km/h. New country: a successful login from a country the user has no located login from in the last 30 days, while it has some from others.
panels.title: New-country logins

panels.description: Countries that logins came from in the time range. LAN and stack-internal addresses have no country.

targets.expr: count(sum by (country_code) (count_over_time({service_name="keycloak-logins", realm=~"$realm"} | json | country_code != "" [$__range]))) or vector(0)

panels.title: Countries

options.content:
**Where logins come from**

Places: [IP Geolocation by DB-IP](https://db-ip.com) (City Lite, CC BY 4.0), looked up on the stack host. LAN and Docker addresses have no place.

panels.description: Logins of the selected realm, newest first. The keycloak-login-tracker service reads the realm's logins from Keycloak's event store every 30 s and writes them to Loki (service_name=keycloak-logins). Country and city come from DB-IP's City Lite database on the stack host (often the ISP's nearest hub, not the exact town); LAN and stack-internal (Docker) addresses have none. Impossible travel: a successful login more than 300 km from the user's previous located login, which it could only have reached faster than 1000 km/h. New country: a successful login from a country the user has no located login from in the last 30 days, while it has some from others. Failed logins are listed but never compared.

targets.expr: {service_name="keycloak-logins", realm=~"$realm"} | json | keep username, result, error, ip, ip_scope, country, city, client_id, flag, prev_location, distance_km, speed_kmh

panels.title: Recent logins

panels.description: Logins from public addresses, at the place DB-IP's City Lite database gives for the address. Red: impossible travel, orange: new country, yellow: failed login, green: the rest. LAN and stack-internal logins have no place and are only in the table. The base map tiles come from Grafana's default map provider; login addresses are not sent anywhere.

targets.expr: {service_name="keycloak-logins", realm=~"$realm"} | json | lat != "" | label_format status=`{{ if .flag }}{{ .flag }}{{ else if eq .result "failed" }}failed{{ else }}ok{{ end }}` | keep username, result, ip, location, lat, lon, flag, status, client_id

panels.title: Login map

panels.description: Successful logins per user and place in the time range. A user who normally signs in from one or two places and shows a new one here is worth a look.

targets.expr: sum by (username, location) (count_over_time({service_name="keycloak-logins", realm=~"$realm", result="success"} | json [$__range]))

panels.title: Places per user

panels.description: The KeycloakLogins alert rules (folder Alerts): impossible travel and new country. Each fires for 10 minutes after a flagged login. No contact point sends them anywhere yet; they show here and in Alerting.
panels.title: Login alerts

panels.description: User events per second from keycloak_user_events_total. Requires KC_EVENT_METRICS_USER_ENABLED.

panels.description: Successful and failed login events per client. client_id is present because KC_EVENT_METRICS_USER_TAGS includes clientId.

targets.expr: sum by (client_id, error) (rate(keycloak_user_events_total{job="$job", realm=~"$realm", event="login", error!=""}[5m]))
